references.text: Jesus' answer to his mother at the wedding in Cana uses the same Greek word for 'time' (kairos) and expresses that his time has not yet come, paralleling the statement in 7:6.
Here Jesus confirms that his time has not yet come while he is speaking in the temple, repeating the motif from 7:6 that his time is determined by the Father.
Here Jesus declares that the 'hour' (kairos) has come for the Son of Man to be glorified, marking that the time which was previously 'not yet come' has now arrived.
The text emphasizes that Jesus knew his time had come to go to the Father, fulfilling the theme of the appointed time discussed in 7:6.
In the prayer, Jesus says, 'Father, the hour has come,' a direct fulfillment of the statement in 7:6 that his time had not yet come earlier but has now arrived.
